items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: he was working with Flem Ferguson and the Washington-Erie Hotel in Shreveport, Louisiana, and he got me on the band there

ctx.x: Well, let's see, that would be after Frank Weinagar Weingard, and I guess that would be around 1930, maybe into '31. And following -- well, we broke up. Beasley started to lose his eyesight and he had to disband the band. Fortunately he didn't lose it. They were able to rectify it. But -- and

that's when I decided to investigate the south. I'd heard so much about all these guys coming out of there, you know, Teagarden and Louis Armstrong out of New Orleans, and so I went -- I got -- I had a friend of mine, a trumpet player who had played in that band that was on the S. S. Pennland, a fellow by the name of Gordon Tulley, and he was working with Flem Ferguson and the Washington-Erie Hotel in Shreveport, Louisiana, and he got me on the band there, and well, that was a delightful job. We -- for our work…
Was that a fairly big hotel?
